newsitem.title: USA: US futures clearing units agree to common banking.
newsitem.headline: US futures clearing units agree to common banking.

text.p: Seven clearing organizations representing all U.S. futures exchanges signed a letter of intent to begin common banking for the first time, the exchanges said Thursday.

Common banking will enable firms doing business on each exchange to settle trades with a single transaction through a common account at a bank, which will cut expenses and reduce credit stress risk to the payment system, the exchanges said in a statement.

Pursuing common banking are: The Chicago Mercantile Exchange, the Board of Trade Clearing Corp, the New York Mercantile Exchange, the Commodity Futures Clearing Corp of New York, the Commodity Clearing Corp, the Kansas City Board of Trade Clearing Corp and the Minneapolis Grain Exchange.
Under the agreement, each firm that is a clearing member of more than one exchange will be able to consolidate banking transactions.
Sid Branson, president of the Commodity Futures Clearing Corp of New York, said he hoped to have an agreement worked out and finalized in the next year.
